chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Dhareer, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said:

A man proposed marriage to a people, so they asked him, 'What is your trade?' He said, 'I sell animals.' So they married him to their daughter, but it turned out that he was selling cats. So they brought the dispute to Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), and he validated his marriage, saying, 'The cats are animals.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on marriage validity if the suitor's specific trade differs from his general description?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and linguistic flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) validates the marriage by interpreting 'selling animals' broadly to include cats. It demonstrates the practical application of general terms (*mutlaq*) in social contracts, emphasizing that unless a specific exclusion is agreed upon, the broader category suffices for validity. This ruling underscores the pragmatic approach of the Imams in facilitating social bonds while maintaining legal precision.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from one of his companions, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn Al Zareer, from Hammad Bin Isa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man sent a proposal to a people, so they said, ‘What is your business?’ so he said, ‘I sell the animals’. So they married to him, and it turned out that he was selling the cats. So they brought the dispute to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> allowed his marriage, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cats are animals’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Darir from Hammad ibn ‘Isa who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his father who has said,

that a man proposed marriage in a family and they asked, ‘What is your business?’ He replied, ‘I sell animals.’ They accepted his proposal and found out that he sells cats, so they took their dispute before ’Amir al- Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who validated the marriage saying that cats are animals.’”
